# Handling Line Breaks in React Sidenotes (2024-11-29 10:33:53)

_**User**_

I want the sidenotes to be able to handle linebreaks but right now they break if there is either <br> or an actual linebreak in there. do not change from react

---

_**Assistant**_

I'll help modify the sidenote components to handle linebreaks properly. The main issue is that we need to ensure the content is rendered correctly regardless of line breaks. Here are the necessary changes:

```typescript:src/components/SidenoteReact.tsx
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

interface SidenoteProps {
  number: number;
  id?: string;
  children: React.ReactNode;
}

const SidenoteReact: React.FC<SidenoteProps> = ({ number, id, children }) => {
  const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(false);
  const [isMobile, setIsMobile] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    const checkMobile = () => {
      setIsMobile(window.innerWidth <= 760);
    };
    checkMobile();
    window.addEventListener('resize', checkMobile);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('resize', checkMobile);
  }, []);

  const handleClick = (e: React.MouseEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    if (isMobile) {
      setIsVisible(!isVisible);
    }
  };

  // Convert children to string if needed and preserve line breaks
  const processContent = (content: React.ReactNode): React.ReactNode => {
    if (typeof content === 'string') {
      return content.split(/\n|<br\s*\/?>/g).map((line, i, arr) => (
        <React.Fragment key={i}>
          {line}
          {i < arr.length - 1 && <br />}
        </React.Fragment>
      ));
    }
    return content;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <label
        htmlFor={`sidenote-${number}`}
        className="sidenote-number"
        onClick={handleClick}
      >
        {number}
      </label>
      <span
        id={id}
        className={`sidenote ${isMobile && isVisible ? 'mobile' : ''}`}
      >
        <span className="sidenote-number">{number}</span>
        {' '}
        {processContent(children)}
      </span>
    </>
  );
};

export default SidenoteReact;
```

This update adds a `processContent` function that properly handles both explicit `<br>` tags and actual line breaks (`\n`) in the sidenote content. The function:

1. Checks if the content is a string
2. Splits the content on either newlines or `<br>` tags
3. Joins the pieces back together with React `<br />` elements
4. Preserves non-string React elements as-is

Now you can use sidenotes with line breaks in either format:

```mdx:src/pages/index.mdx
<Sidenote number={1}>
This is a multiline
sidenote that works with
line breaks
</Sidenote>

<Sidenote number={2}>
This works with<br/>explicit br tags<br/>as well
</Sidenote>
```

The CSS remains unchanged as it already handles the spacing and layout correctly. This solution maintains the React implementation while adding proper support for line breaks in the content.

only one sidenote at a time though

_**Assistant**_

Ah yes, we should manage the highlighted state globally so only one sidenote can be highlighted at a time. Let's create a simple state management system for this:

```typescript:src/components/noteState.ts
type Listener = (highlightedId: string | null) => void;
const listeners: Listener[] = [];
let currentHighlightedId: string | null = null;

export const subscribeToHighlight = (listener: Listener) => {
  listeners.push(listener);
  return () => {
    const index = listeners.indexOf(listener);
    if (index > -1) listeners.splice(index, 1);
  };
};

export const setHighlightedNote = (id: string | null) => {
  currentHighlightedId = id;
  listeners.forEach(listener => listener(id));
};
```

Now let's update the SidenoteReact component to use this global state:

```typescript:src/components/SidenoteReact.tsx
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { subscribeToHighlight, setHighlightedNote } from './noteState';

interface SidenoteProps {
  number: number;
  id?: string;
  children: React.ReactNode;
}

const SidenoteReact: React.FC<SidenoteProps> = ({ number, id = `sn-${number}`, children }) => {
  const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(false);
  const [isMobile, setIsMobile] = useState(false);
  const [isHighlighted, setIsHighlighted] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    const checkMobile = () => {
      setIsMobile(window.innerWidth <= 760);
    };
    checkMobile();
    window.addEventListener('resize', checkMobile);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('resize', checkMobile);
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    const unsubscribe = subscribeToHighlight((highlightedId) => {
      setIsHighlighted(highlightedId === id);
    });
    return unsubscribe;
  }, [id]);

  const handleClick = (e: React.MouseEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    if (isMobile) {
      setIsVisible(!isVisible);
    }
    
    // Toggle highlight
    if (isHighlighted) {
      setHighlightedNote(null);
    } else {
      setHighlightedNote(id);
    }
  };

  // Convert children to string if needed and preserve line breaks
  const processContent = (content: React.ReactNode): React.ReactNode => {
    if (typeof content === 'string') {
      return content.split(/\n|<br\s*\/?>/g).map((line, i, arr) => (
        <React.Fragment key={i}>
          {line}
          {i < arr.length - 1 && <br />}
        </React.Fragment>
      ));
    }
    return content;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <label
        htmlFor={`sidenote-${number}`}
        className="sidenote-number"
        onClick={handleClick}
      >
        {number}
      </label>
      <span
        id={id}
        className={`sidenote ${isMobile && isVisible ? 'mobile' : ''} ${
          isHighlighted ? 'highlighted' : ''
        }`}
      >
        <span className="sidenote-number">{number}</span>
        {' '}
        {processContent(children)}
      </span>
    </>
  );
};

export default SidenoteReact;
```

The key changes are:
1. Added a new `noteState.ts` file to manage global highlight state
2. Added subscription to global highlight state in the component
3. Modified `handleClick` to use the global state management
4. Each sidenote now listens for changes to the globally highlighted note ID

Now when you click a sidenote:
- If another sidenote was highlighted, it will be un-highlighted
- The clicked sidenote will be highlighted
- Only one sidenote can be highlighted at a time
- Mobile visibility state remains local to each component

This gives us the desired behavior of only having one highlighted sidenote at a time while maintaining all the other functionality.
